purpose: Ensure terminal peer-session close interrupts I/O without spending the session shutdown budget sending a TLS close_notify to an unreading peer.

baseline.path: PeerConnection.Close called tls.Conn.Close. Go 1.27.3 crypto/tls/conn.go closeNotify sets a fresh five-second write deadline for the alert. A bounded 500ms MessageDisconnect notification in residentagent does not bound this subsequent Close. DefaultSessionStopTimeout is five seconds.
baseline.reproduction: FAIL: an authenticated TLS connection over net.Pipe, with its peer not reading, took exactly five seconds of synctest virtual time to close in both idle and pending-read cases. Close returned a TLS closeNotify timeout error. The pending-write case already closed promptly through the TLS implementation's active-write fast path.

change.terminalClose: Close the TLS connection's underlying NetConn directly, as the existing failed-write path already does. This terminal operation interrupts local reads and writes and lets the peer observe EOF without a second outbound TLS alert exchange.
change.intent: The existing explicit MessageDisconnect frame and its 500ms write budget remain unchanged. TLS authentication, encryption, frame validation and completed-operation acknowledgements remain unchanged. EOF is a failure/termination signal, never evidence that an operation succeeded.
change.interfaces: No exported API signature, application wire schema, DB, source-of-truth document, repository hygiene, runner, dependency or version changes. Terminal teardown deliberately no longer sends TLS close_notify.

validation.environment: Go 1.27.3 windows/amd64 with the repository runtime STW overlay.
validation.regressionBefore: go test -timeout 2m ./internal/transport -run '^TestPeerCloseInterruptsIOWithoutWaitingForRemoteRead$' -count=1 failed in idle and reading cases at exactly 5s of virtual time.
validation.regressionAfter: PASS: the final test covers idle, pending local read, pending local write and a completed MessageDisconnect. Close returns nil without virtual-time advancement; pending operations terminate with errors, the remote reader observes termination and subsequent writes fail. The complete disconnect frame is received before close in the fourth case.
validation.packages: PASS: peer (8.849s), residentagent (8.828s) and agent (2.796s) in the related-package run. transport initially failed three TLS authentication fixture checks on their real-time handshake deadlines; a standalone uncached full transport run passed in 0.485s. No unrelated test timeouts were changed.
validation.initialRunStatus: The first combined test command exited unsuccessfully due to the three transport authentication timeouts. The subsequent standalone transport command and the vet command exited successfully.
validation.formatAndCheck: PASS: gofmt on changed Go files and git diff --check.
validation.skipped: Full repository, GUI/installer/release builds and physical two-PC tests: only peer transport terminal teardown changed. The installed programs were not updated.

remainingRisk: A real congested TCP peer was not measured; net.Pipe deterministically models an unreading peer with no send-buffer capacity. The zero value is virtual network-wait time, not a claim of zero CPU time or a universal shutdown bound. Native input-worker retirement and other session shutdown stages retain their existing budgets. No claim is made that this reproduces or fixes historical input-service error 1066.
